rows.title: [Desktop] Unobserved MCP extension-host query is evicted after 5 minutes, retaining old sessions and spawning new MCP processes
rows.platform: Windows 11 Home 25H2, build 26200.9168, x64; native Windows backend. Requested PowerShell output: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64.

analysis.title: [Desktop] Unobserved MCP extension-host query is evicted after 5 minutes, retaining old sessions and spawning new MCP processes
analysis.subtopic: MCP extension-host query cache eviction leaks threads and processes
analysis.summary: The Desktop renderer's MCP extension-host query has staleTime: Infinity but no gcTime override, causing the cache entry to be garbage-collected after 5 minutes on the imperative (unobserved) path. Cache eviction does not send thread/unsubscribe, so the old session and its MCP processes remain loaded while a new session is spawned, leading to duplicate process accumulation and eventual app-server request queue exhaustion that blocks message submission.
analysis.userScenario: Using Codex Desktop normally while MCP extension-host processes accumulate silently due to query-cache garbage collection without unsubscribe, eventually filling the app-server request queue and blocking message submission.
analysis.userImpact: Message submission fails with 'App server request queue is full' and 'request expired while queued' errors due to accumulated duplicate MCP sessions exhausting server capacity.
analysis.scopeReason: The issue directly concerns the Codex Desktop app's internal MCP extension-host query-cache lifecycle, thread management, and process accumulation — all core Codex functionality.
